verdict: Do not adopt the measured batched compile-then-run variant in production. It was slower on the complete measured cold shard.

provenance.environment: one standard ubuntu-24.04 GitHub-hosted job; separate empty build caches; shared prefetched modules; fresh pinned PostgreSQL before each phase; baseline then candidate

allowed_skip.reason: release fixture job supplies pinned COSIGN_BIN

limitations: One cold AB pair, without reverse-order replication.
Candidate inherits warm image/page-cache effects despite separate initially empty compiler caches.
Database reset cost differs because baseline pulls the pinned container image first.
Single predetermined Linux shard at product source 48189fff; not current-main whole-suite or PR-latency evidence.
Same-runner comparison excludes cross-runner binary upload/download, scheduling, and authenticity overhead; adding those cannot improve this measured variant.
Process elapsed sums overlap and are not runner minutes. Runner allocation is measured elapsed occupancy, not a monetary charge.
